thread.title: Time to talk rentals townwide impact
thread.title_full: Time to talk rentals townwide impact

author: ohtadmin
title: Time to talk rentals townwide impact
text:
To the editor:
The town council recently approved 122 short-term rental applications for 2026. People who opposed a certain application, could have voiced their concerns at that meeting.
But what if you are opposed to the entire process being used in this application process? The residents of Jamestown need to have a larger voice in the issue of short-term rentals as a whole.
It already has been pointed out short-term rentals are disruptive to communities as they typically use more of our limited resources, create quality-of life-problems in residential neighborhoods, displace much-needed year-round rental units, and increase housing prices virtually shutting everyone but the wealthy out of the market.
This is a business that is basically deregulated as it does not have to adhere to laws like other lodging establishments, such as bed and breakfasts, nor is it required to adhere to zoning laws as these businesses operate in residential areas.
These are just some of the issues that need to be discussed in greater depth before the town continues to approve more short-term rentals.
When the council members were running for election, I spoke with most of the candidates and asked how many year-round rentals currently exist on the island. None of them knew. I wondered how council members could move forward to approve short-term rentals without this information. It begs the question, what does guide the council’s decision to approve an application?
We have yet to have an in-depth discussion about whether the community — not just the investors — really benefits from these rentals. This is a dialogue long overdue. The community needs to work with the council to set up parameters for short-term rentals in order to guarantee the decisions being made are transparent and in the best interest of the island as a whole.
Mary Forman
Bayberry Road
